notes: Historical definitions: revenue = total revenues; EBIT = operating income; D&A = 'Depreciation, amortization, and other' from the consolidated income statement; capex = 'Capital and technology expenditures' from the consolidated cash flow statement. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

NWC build (modeling choice): NWC = (Accounts and notes receivable + Prepaid expenses and other) - (Accounts payable + Accrued payroll and benefits + Liability for guest loyalty program + Accrued expenses and other), excluding cash and excluding current portion of long-term debt. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

Investments/minority interest/p preferred equity: set to null for 'investments' due to ambiguity on which line items your DCF pipeline expects as 'investments' (could include contract acquisition costs/loan advances/other investing cash flows). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

Comps: EV/NTM Revenue and EV/NTM EBITDA use StockAnalysis EV/Sales and EV/EBITDA ratios as proxies because the cited dataset does not explicitly label them as NTM. ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/hlt/statistics/))

Tax and NOLs: tax_rate is a normalized assumption; NOL balance taken from the 2025 filing, and NOL utilization percent is an assumption (not directly disclosed at the utilization level). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))
Market inputs: current_price sourced from live market quote (MAR) as of 2026-03-21.

catalysts: Upside from RevPAR and net room growth tracking to the high end of FY2026 guidance ranges. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))

Further acceleration in operating leverage if owned/leased mix and operating expenses track toward improved EBIT margins. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

Sustained shareholder returns (management >$4.3B capital returns in 2026) supporting sentiment and valuation multiples. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))
company_overview: Fee-driven, asset-light model: franchise fees plus base and incentive management fees (with additional owned/leased and cost reimbursement revenue). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

2025 system momentum: net rooms grew over 4.3% and the worldwide development pipeline reached ~4,100 properties / ~610,000 rooms. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))

Marriott Bonvoy membership neared ~271 million at year-end 2025. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marriott-international-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-302683152.html))
current_context: FY2025 performance: worldwide RevPAR +2.0% (Q4 RevPAR +1.9%); asset-light model continued to generate substantial cash enabling >$4.0B of capital returns in 2025. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marriott-international-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-302683152.html))

FY2026 outlook (management guidance): worldwide RevPAR +1.5% to 2.5%, net rooms +4.5% to 5%, adjusted EBITDA growth +8% to 10%, and >$4.3B capital returns to shareholders. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))
Management also expects investment spending of ~$1.0B–$1.1B in 2026. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth chains to 2026–2030 topline assumptions consistent with management’s FY2026 RevPAR and net room growth ranges. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))

EBIT margin modeled to stay within a narrow band around the recent operating margin history (2023–2025). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

Capex intensity normalized to reflect ongoing technology and owned/leased renovation needs while separating out broader 'investment spending' from pure capex modeling. ([fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company-assets/729/quartr/earnings-release-8-k-909ff-2026-02-10-12-08-01.pdf))

Working-capital modeling reflects negative net working capital driven by the guest loyalty program and payables/other accruals (included in the chosen NWC build). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))
key_risks: Macro and demand risk: softer transient/business travel (and/or weaker international leisure/cross-border demand) could pressure RevPAR. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/marriott-international-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-302683152.html))
Tax rate volatility and NOL realization risk could impact effective cash taxes and valuation. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

Execution risk in technology transformation and related timing of spending and reimbursements could delay margin/cash outcomes. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1048286/000104828626000007/mar-20251231.htm))

The forecast revenue growth profile declines modestly from 2026 levels, consistent with normalization after cyclical demand recovery.
